name: Cotton thread making at Neolithic Mehrgarh
summary: People at Neolithic Mehrgarh in Balochistan were using cotton thread in the sixth millennium BCE, the oldest cotton known in the Indian subcontinent.
description: Several threads preserved by mineralisation inside a copper bead from a Neolithic burial at Mehrgarh were identified as cotton, genus Gossypium, by reflected-light and scanning electron microscopy. The find shows cotton fibre being worked into thread in the sixth millennium BCE; it does not show woven cloth, and the authors could not tell whether the cotton was already domesticated. They take the evidence from Balochistan and the Indus valley to support a South Asian origin for one of the Old World cottons.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited page: cotton cloth from South Asia came to clothe the subcontinent and was traded and copied across Asia, Africa and Europe (depth 2), and calico printing and mechanised spinning grew from the effort to match it (generativity 2); reach is held at 2, not the lead's 3, because cotton was taken up separately in the Americas and Africa and the lower score is taken when torn.

date.label: 6th millennium BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Threads preserved by mineralisation in a copper bead from a Neolithic burial at Mehrgarh, dated to the 6th millennium BCE, were identified as cotton.

evidence.supports: several threads preserved by mineralization in a copper bead from a Neolithic burial (6th millennium) at Mehrgarh, Pakistan, were subject to rigorous metallurgical analysis. Under this new microscopic procedure, the fibres were identiﬁed as cotton (genus Gossypium ).
evidence.locator: Second paragraph of the page's summary of Moulherat et al. 2002

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Check the 2002 Journal of Archaeological Science article itself for the date and wording; this card uses Harappa.com's summary with extracts, and the publisher's page could not be opened.
No source opened dates woven cotton cloth at Mohenjo-daro or Harappa; find one and add it as a later event.
Huaca Prieta cotton textiles of about 6,200 years ago (ScienceDaily, 2016) are a separate origin and need their own record.
The page mentions cotton string at Shahi Tump (4th millennium) and woven cotton at Dhuweila in Jordan (4th millennium), not yet followed up.
The Mehrgarh coordinates are recalled and should be checked against an archaeological source.

research.note: The page calls this the oldest known cotton in the Indian subcontinent and an earlier use of cotton than was known before; the oldest New World cotton textile opened for comparison (Huaca Prieta, Peru, about 6,200 years old, in a 2016 George Washington University release on ScienceDaily) is at least several centuries later. No source opened says outright that it is the oldest in the world, and cotton was domesticated separately in the Americas.
